newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong and Tokyo lag as most Asian bourses rise.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong and Tokyo lag as most Asian bourses rise.

text.p: Tokyo and Hong Kong sounded the only sour notes in Friday trading as most other Asian markets posted moderate gains.

The Dow Jones Industrial Index's close above the 6,300-point mark in New York trading overnight appeared to have little impact on the region, however, although it did fuel a record performance in Australian shares.
But brokers said most other bourses advanced on a variety of local factors.

Tokyo stocks gained early in the morning on the Dow's rise, brokers said, but gave ground again in the afternoon. Brokers said unclear market direction, thin trade and position-squaring ahead of the weekend dragged the indices down in the afternoon.
The 225-share Nikkei ended down 101.31 points, or 0.48 percent, at 20,929.73.
The index had climbed to as high as 21,159 in the morning on the Dow's record high and expectations of buying by public funds.
Hong Kong stocks snapped a five-day winning streak to end sharply lower as investors locked in profits following a week of record highs, brokers said.
The Hang Seng index closed 115.43 points or 0.89 percent lower at 12,889.37 after hitting a new record intra-day high during the session of 13,054.91.
"Profit-taking pressures increased above the 13,000 level," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities. The Hang Seng broke above that level for the first time on Thursday.
"Today we are having a consolidation but the market still looks good," said one trader.
Australian shares closed at a record high inspired by the Dow. The All Ordinaries index climbed 24.8 points, or 1.05 percent, to 2,387.3. The index touched an intra-day all-time high of 2,391.2.
"The Dow has finally installed confidence in our market and subsequently we saw buying across the board from local and offshore investors today," said one broker.

Seoul stocks also closed higher in a broad-based technical rebound following recent sharp declines, brokers said. But they said the market's underlying sentiment remained bearish under pressure from a high level of margin loans.
The composite stock index ended 7.26 points higher at a provisional 750.29, a rise of 0.98 percent.
The Thai stock index ended above the 1,000-point key resistance level in busy trade as investors snapped up shares ahead of Sunday's election, brokers said.

The SET index closed 10.11 points or 1.02 percent higher at 1,000.73. One analyst said speculation that the Democrat Party might win Sunday's general election emboldened investors on the belief that its strong economic team could help salvage the slowing economy.
Singapore shares fought off profit-takers to end steady. Dealers said market sentiment was still firm and several rounds of selling were well absorbed.
The Straits Times Industrials index ended at 2,193.64, up 3.88 points, or 0.18 percent.
Jakarta stocks surged on the combined effect of sharp rises in shares of heavyweight Telkom and some banking stocks coupled with the presence of fresh funds.
The Jakarta Composite Index jumped 15.98 points, or 2.66 percent, to 616.89 points in active trading.
At 1115 GMT, the dollar traded at 111.15/1.20 yen and 1.5064/74 marks.
Hong Kong gold prices ended down on heavy sales from Europe just before the market close. Bullion fell to US$380.40/90 an ounce against New York's close on Thursday at US$381.00/40.
SIMEX Brent crude futures fell. The January contract ended at $23.48 per barrel, down 12 cents from London's Thursday close.
